title: That Tallow Balm That Smells Like a Ripe Pear: My Weirdly Good Skin Thing
body:
Okay so. I was just sitting there, my hands were like sandpaper. It was spring but my skin didn't get the memo. I’d tried the lotion from the drugstore, the fancy one my sister gave me, the stuff in the blue bottle. Nothing. My knuckles looked like a dried-up riverbed. Weird.

Then I saw this thing online. A tallow balm. Beef fat. For your skin. I know. It sounds like something you’d use to grease a pan, not your face. But the pictures looked nice. And it said “Pear.” I like pears. I was tired. I clicked buy. It came in this little jar from some shop on Etsy, made in France apparently. I opened the box and just stared at it for a day. Beef tallow balm. Huh.

Anyway, one night my hands were so bad I just went for it. Unscrewed the lid. First thought: Oh. That’s actually… nice.

It doesn’t smell like beef. Thank god. It doesn’t smell like a candle or perfume either. It smells like you just cut into a really good, juicy pear. Not candy pear. Real pear. The kind that’s perfectly ripe, sweet but not too sweet, with that fresh, clean smell. It’s light. It’s just… pleasant. It made the whole beef fat thing way less intimidating. This pear tallow balm just sat there smelling innocent and fruity.

I scooped a little. The texture is weird. In a good way. It’s solid but soft, like cold butter, but then it just melts the second it touches your skin. Doesn’t feel greasy. It just… disappears. My sandpaper hands drank it up. I sat there smelling my palms like a weirdo. Just pears. And my skin felt calm. Not oily. Just not screaming for once.

## Why I Even Tried Beef Tallow Skincare

Look, I was desperate. And curious. I read that tallow—this specific whipped beef tallow balm—is made from grass-fed cow fat, whipped up until it’s fluffy. They say it’s really close to the oils our own skin makes. So it gets it. It doesn’t just sit on top like a plastic wrap. It goes in. My skin barrier was clearly on strike, so I figured, what’s the worst that could happen? It’s just fat. People have been using animal fats on skin forever, right? Before all the chemical stuff in bottles.

I started with my hands. Then one morning, my face felt tight and sad. I was out of my usual moisturizer. I looked at the jar of this natural pear skincare stuff. Thought, well, in for a penny. I put a tiny bit on my cheeks and forehead. Braced for a breakout. For it to feel gross.

It didn’t. It felt like nothing. In a good way. My face just felt… normal. Hydrated. Not shiny. Just quiet. I kept doing it. It became the thing I reached for when my skin felt off. Dry patch on my elbow? Pear tallow balm. Rough heels? Yep. It’s this one-jar solution that lives on my bedside table now.

## What This Pear Scented Tallow Balm Actually Does

It’s not magic. It’s just really good at one thing: making my skin not hate me. The pear scent is the gateway drug. It makes using it a tiny little moment of nice. You open the jar, get that whiff of fresh fruit, and it doesn’t feel like a chore. It feels like a treat. A very simple, weird treat involving rendered cow fat. Life is strange.

I use it at night mostly. After I wash my face. I scoop a pea-sized amount, warm it between my fingers, and just press it into my skin. It’s become this little ritual. The scent is gentle and sophisticated in its simplicity—it’s just pear. It’s hydrating in a deep way, not a surface slick. In the morning, my skin feels balanced. Not oily, not dry. My hands, which used to crack and bleed if I looked at them wrong, are just… hands now. Normal skin hands. It’s wild.

I got one for my mom too. She has psoriasis on her arms. She was skeptical. “You put what on your face?” But she tried it. She texted me last week: “My spots are less angry.” That’s high praise from her.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

So I’ve been using this pear tallow balm for a while now. I’m almost out, which means I need to order another one from that Etsy shop soon. The results are… subtle but real. I don’t have a dramatic before-and-after. My skin hasn’t turned into a baby’s bottom. But it’s settled down. The constant dryness on my cheeks is gone. The random redness I’d get? Minimized. My hands are presentable. I don’t think about my skin as much. It’s just there, doing its job, not causing problems.

That’s the biggest thing. It’s not a high-maintenance product. It’s a little jar of quiet help. The pear scent makes it feel a bit special, but the tallow is what does the work. It mimics human sebum, so it absorbs deep. It doesn’t clog me up. It just reinforces whatever my skin is supposed to be doing on its own. I used to have a shelf full of products. Now I have like, three things. This balm is one of them.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Yeah, surprisingly. The idea freaked me out too. But it makes sense—it’s really similar to the oils our skin already produces. So it absorbs well and helps repair your skin barrier instead of just masking dryness. My face seems to think it’s good.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not for me, and I can get clogged pores pretty easy. Because it’s so similar to our own skin stuff, it sinks in instead of sitting on top and blocking things. It’s the opposite of greasy. It just… melds.

**What does the pear tallow balm smell like?**
Honestly? Like a fresh, ripe pear. Not artificial. Not super strong. Just a clean, light, fruity smell that makes the whole experience feel nice and not medicinal. It’s the main reason I reach for it over the unscented one.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, feeling dry or rough or just generally pissed off, this might be worth a shot. I didn’t expect much from a scented tallow balm review situation, but here I am, about to buy jar number two. My skin’s happy. I’m happy. And I smell faintly of pears. It’s a win.
